## 2026-10-10 000 DECISION: parallel source tasks write per-source staging files, consolidated once by task 211
    The seven growth leads (204-210) all run in one wave; if each wrote the shared data/catalog/extras.jsonl,
    data/commons/files.jsonl, classified.jsonl, web/data/plans.json and web/data/sites.json they would collide
    (the driver replays the schedule when shared files make tasks wait). Each source task therefore writes only
    its own extras_<src>.jsonl / files_<src>.jsonl / classified_<src>.jsonl plus its fit/src_<src>.py module;
    211 (wave 3) consolidates into the canonical files GOAL.md names, then runs build_catalog.py and
    tools/export_plans.py once. Same reason the batch (203a/b) writes only platefits docs + review items and
    212 alone runs the page-facing plan_fit sync (depictions + drawings counts in sites.json + the review list).

## 2026-10-10 000 DECISION: the batch is 203 (parent, split) with subtasks 203a (US) / 203b (rest of world)
    One batch over 384 sites is too big for one task and a single batch module would block wave 3 (211) behind
    it; splitting by region keeps 203b and 211 in the same wave (disjoint files). The parent's boxes are covered
    jointly by the two subtasks; the parent returns when both are done.

# Task 001 fit-gate

## 2026-10-10 001 DECISION: the gate judges by metric conjunction, not by one score
Recon spikes (no code in the repo yet; scripts in /tmp, results in the task hand-over): (1) ALL-ink 4-neighbour
ridge contrast on the DEM fails (castle-rising true fit scored worst, -0.653 vs null -0.07); (2) autowalls-extracted
wall template + fit_plate's stroke-normal contrast separates true from 60 m/10°/15% on castle-rising but NOT on
bergues (flat town, ploughed walls: true -0.205 worst), and its one-sidedness lets any template score +0.53 on
hilly cross-site ground; (3) old-map ink proximity is saturated on dense maps. So the gate will combine: pair-
consistency residuals, old-map correlation (spike 4, pending), DEM-vs-search-matched-null where relief is strong.
Chosen over a single relief score because docs/autofit.md finding 2 already proved the relief score has false
peaks; the 4th wrong-fit type (best placement on another site's ground) is constructed to beat any single-score
gate, so evidence must be independent per layer.

## 2026-10-10 001 DECISION: held-out selection and test strategy
Held-out = 8 of the 21 fits by numpy.random.default_rng(20260101).choice over sorted filenames (to be written in
docs/gate.md before the run); the other 13 are the dev set for threshold selection only. Test re-run strategy:
commit per-fit input caches as data/gate/*.npz (DEM, map ink, plate ink, wall template, pairs) so the test is
offline and deterministic; the gate program itself fetches DEMs at runtime when its cache is absent. .npy is
gitignored globally but .npz is not (only data/autofit/*.npz is).

## 2026-10-10 001 BLOCKER: none yet - design iteration, not a repeated failure
Attempts so far are distinct metric experiments (spikes 1-3 failed, spike 4 pending), each with a different cause;
not a stuck blocker. If spike 4 (old-map correlation) also fails to separate the four wrong-fit types, next
candidate: placement-centre-vs-catalog-position + plate-extent-vs-site-box checks for the cross-site type.

## 2026-10-10 001 DECISION: held-out set moves to seed 20260108 - seeds 20260101-0107 all overlap the design set
The hand-over planned `default_rng(20260101).choice` over "21 sorted docs" but there are 20 docs (hand-over
miscounted: 19 sites, old-sarum has 2). Seeds 20260101-20260107 all place at least one of the four design fits

Procedure now fixed and to be recorded in docs/gate.md: try seeds 20260101, 20260102, ... in ascending order;
the first seed whose rng.choice(20, 8, replace=False) over the sorted doc names is disjoint from the design set

## 2026-10-10 001 DECISION: pair-consistency residuals alone cannot be the gate - dev true fits are sloppy
Solved-transform per-pair residuals on the 12 DEV fits (held-out untouched): medians 3.7-53.1 m, maxes
4.6-86.7 m (old-sarum c_8192: 53.1/86.7; hembury 40.3/53.3; little-solsbury 46.8/65.0; bergues 29.9/51.7;
castle-rising 12.0/19.0; mayburgh/mound-bottom/serpent-mound/whitley tight, < 11 m). A 60 m move (60 m per
point) and cross-site (km-scale) are caught by any threshold above the dev max, but 10 deg / x1.15 add only
~0.1745 r / 0.15 r per point (~9/15 m on a 100 m-radius site) - inside the dev true-fit spread. So residuals
are the 60 m / cross-site layer of the conjunction; rotation/scale need the image conjunct (spike 6 dir_frac
is the candidate, run in progress).

## 2026-10-10 001 DECISION: all six image-structure metrics fail (spikes 1-6) - the gate pivots to pure geometry
Spike 4 (blurred plate-ink vs blurred map-ink Pearson): castle-rising true +0.386 < null_max +0.424; bergues true
+0.052 < null +0.484; maiden-castle true -0.048 < null +0.411 (mirrored +0.379); serpent-mound true -0.111 <
null +0.645. Cross-site searches scored +0.653 and +0.972 - dense maps correlate with anything. FAIL.
Spike 5 (autowalls wall points within 10 m of density-filtered map strokes): no separation at any site
(castle-rising true 0.718 vs moved 0.720 / x0.85 0.841; bergues off-grid; mirrored is the only case killed). FAIL.
Spike 6 (same but requiring the wall normal to align with the stroke across-direction, |cos| >= 0.7, 15 m
window): castle-rising true 0.420 vs x0.85 0.450 (wrong HIGHER); bergues true 0.056 (only 23% of its wall points
in-box) with all cases 0.03-0.06; maiden-castle true 0.259 vs x0.85 0.331; serpent-mound true 0.252 vs x1.15
0.338. Cross-site: castle plate on bergues map 0.457 (> bergues's own true). corr_ws returned n/a everywhere.
FAIL. Combined with spikes 1-3 (DEM ridge, DEM wall contrast, ink proximity - see archive), no image statistic
separates 60 m / 10 deg / 15% / cross-site on dense old maps, because those shifts (<= 0.1745 r, 0.15 r, 60 m)
are smaller than the map's structural wavelength. The gate will therefore be geometric: pair-residual magnitude
catches 60 m move (median exactly 60 m vs dev max 53.1 m) and cross-site (km-scale), and a residual-vs-radius
pattern (10 deg / x1.15 add 0.1745 r / 0.15 r per point, a radial gradient a true sloppy fit does not have)
must catch rotation/scale. Spike 7 (next session): measure those statistics on the 12 dev docs and the four
wrong types to set thresholds. The gate stays image-free -> no skimage, no requirements.txt change needed.

## 2026-10-10 001 DECISION: spike 7 done - conjunction frozen: reject if med>45 m OR slope_o>0.145 OR (slope_o>0.11 AND io<-10 m)
Spike 7 (/tmp/spike_gate7.py, /tmp/spike7_out.txt): 12 dev docs x {true, moved 60 m NE, turned 10 deg about the
placement centroid, scaled x1.15, cross-site re-centre onto the next dev site's box centre}, scored as
|placement - anchor| (ground m, k=cos(lat0); anchors = the doc's own pairs; true case = solved transform vs own
pairs, verified identical to the canonical depictions fit.resid_m: bergues 18.8/32.6, berkhamsted 17.4/21.8,
old-sarum c_8192 33.3/54.4 - the old hand-over's 53.1/86.7 etc. were Web-Mercator m = these x1.59). Results:
true med 2.2-33.3 (all pass med>45); moved med 59.1-68.5 and xsite 19 km-7700 km (all killed by med>45, margin
~30% both sides); rot10 slope_o 0.1747-0.230 (all killed by slope_o>0.145; 2sin5 deg pins the floor); scale15
slope_o 0.130-0.240 with the MASS at 0.130-0.141 BELOW the 0.15 theory (through-origin OLS is attenuated by
the anchor noise at n=3-6) -> the two-clause pattern test: slope_o>0.145 OR (slope_o>0.11 AND io<-10 m, io =
inner-half minus outer-half mean residual). Dev outcome: 48 wrong -> 2 accepted (castle-rising scale15:
med 15.8/slope 0.141/io -8.7; whitley scale15: med 11.7/slope 0.136/io -7.4 = 1 in 24 <= 1 in 20) and 12 true ->
10 accepted (rejected: berkhamsted slope 0.230, old-sarum c_8192 slope 0.161+io -20.3 - both have a genuinely
radial own-residual pattern, indistinguishable from a scale error at n=4-5). Thin margins (calleva scale15
io -10.1 vs -10; castle-rising slope 0.141 vs 0.145) are inherent to n=3-6 and must NOT be re-tuned on the
held-out set: if the one-shot run shows more than 1-in-20 wrong acceptance, document the numbers in gate.md and
let the review queue backstop, per the acceptance criteria. The gate's production contract: score the model's
claimed placement against its recorded anchor pairs; a consistent global error (anchors AND placement both off)
passes by pure geometry - documented limit, backstopped by GOAL's 18/20 human sample. Next: commit docs/gate.md
(pre-registration: 20260108 partition, the rule, the four recipes, reproduce command) BEFORE any held-out look,
then pipeline/fit_gate.py, tools/gate_heldout.py (one-shot run -> table in gate.md), tests/test_gate.py (offline
golden re-run, no ports, project+tmp writes only).

## 2026-10-10 200 DECISION: the P180 live route was broken (HTML scraping); replaced with a batched API route (local M<pageid> items, normalized-global chase), P6216 excluded
Where: fit/evidence.py (fetch_page_ids, fetch_file_entities, live_evidence, record_live; fetch_file_item and the UA constant deleted), the depicts bullet of the module docstring, check_depicts
Probing before the first live run (per the iteration-12 plan) showed the old fetch_file_item was wrong in
two ways: (1) the item-QID patterns (ItemPage/(Q\d+), "wikibaseItem", "globalItem") match nothing, because
old file pages carry only a LOCAL MediaInfo entity - the page's mw.config has "wbEntityId":"M<page id>"
(M37646731 for the probe file) and the embedded JSON is that local entity's statements; (2) the P180|P6216
regex matched P6216 *license* statements (Q19652 "public domain") and reported them as depicts values, and
the only Q ids in the page at all were Q13414952 (MD5 - a P459 qualifier on the file's hash statement) and
the license. So the route would have mis-recorded licenses as depictions and never found a real file item.
Fix, verified with live probes: fetch_page_ids (action=query prop=info, 50/batch) gives the page id;
fetch_file_entities then calls the Commons API wbgetentities with ids=M<pid> (the "site" parameter is
rejected by the API but unnecessary; the local wiki returns the entity under "statements", not "claims")
in batches of 50, and for pages whose local entity normalizes to a global item ({"normalized":{"item":"Q…"}}
+ missing) it chases that Q id through the Wikidata service. Only P180 is read as a depiction; P6216 was
also removed from check_depicts (it is a license, never a depicts). The recorded "file_qid" is the item id
actually used (M for local, Q for global). The probe files had no P180 at all, which foreshadowed the
corpus-wide result (next entry).

Where: fit/evidence.py (record, record_live, live_evidence, resolve_places), data/commons/files.jsonl, tasks/200-evidence.md, tasks/801-evidence-no-tie-coverage.md

categories/claims/entities/HTML per row (1338 x 4+ requests, hours, and an all-or-nothing rewrite at the
end). Now record_live prefetches once for all pending rows (file categories 50/batch, site claims 50/batch
for 164 unique qids, page ids 50/batch, file entities 50/batch, place searches per unique name with one
batched claims fetch, subcats lazily per site category and cached across rows) and computes each row's
evidence offline from that context (live_evidence - no network in the row loop), flushing files.jsonl in
chunks of 25 so an interrupted run keeps progress (a rerun skips rows on rec == "evidence/1"). The full run
took well under an hour, hit no 429s (commons.get's Retry-After backoff stood by unused), and finished:
825 category, 164 caption_coords, 38 hand_tied (earlier), 354 none (74 with stored conflicts, 280 plain
no-tie). Result: every one of the 1381 titled commons rows + all 890 book rows carries evidence with
specifics and a checked date (box 1); check exits 0 (1162 pass / 0 fail / 1109 no-tie) with the 74
conflict rows stored none-with-conflict, never pass (box 3, real-data confirmation; the sample golden

Corrections and traps found while doing this (they change how the next session reads the prep):
1. **The plan_fit worker in the temp tree dies at `import plan_fit`, not at the missing scan.**
   conftest copies no pipeline/ directory at all, so the worker's first import is a

   which conftest never reads again - harmless, tiny). The prep's case-3 wording "the worker fails
   on the missing scan and is swallowed" assumed pipeline/ was copied - it is not. Behavior the

   changes (a 374-file sha256 snapshot - every platefits doc + every depictions.json - verified
   byte-identical before/after except the one new doc). The test gives the worker 4 s of bounded
   liveness polling (GET / every 0.5 s) rather than awaiting it.

   EFFIGY MOUND" etc. The committed probe reads textContent (raw DOM case) and the test lowercases
   both sides before matching phrases - do not switch back to innerText with case-sensitive asserts.
3. **saveFit crop math: size is [w, h] (2 elements), map_box is 4 (x1, y1, x2, y2).** crop =
   [x1*w, y1*h, x2*w, y2*h] (same as openPlan). A first dry-run script multiplied element-wise and
   hit IndexError; the test builds the crop correctly.

   KeyError'd on `item["no_picture"]` once; the test's seed helper passes

   - it bit this session twice. Kill stray scratch servers by PID from `ps aux | grep -F serve.py`
   instead.

   test is the primary determinism check.

   regex was fixed for all three. "N unit to the inch" rows with a parenthetical ("2 Ch. (352 Ft.)",
   "12 Rods 200 feet") take the FIRST quantity. Optional polish left: reorder inch alternations to
   (?:inches|inch|in) in the two regexes (no current corpus value needs it).

## 2026-10-11 203a DECISION: the 001 gate is a pure-statistics one-shot - R1 resolved, adapter is thin
The prep notes (R1) inferred an ink/DEM conjunct gate; the MERGED 001 is different: fit_gate.gate(pairs,
transform=None) -> (verdict, stats {n, med, slope_o, io}) - numpy only, no images, no network
(docs/gate.md s.2). So the batch needs no fail-closed gate inputs, no DEM, no old-map ink. The adapter
fit/batch_us.py gate_placement solves plan_fit.similarity from the model's pairs, scores the claimed
placement against the recorded anchors, and records the gate's median residual (m) as the doc's score.
Caveat (by design, docs/gate.md s.7): when the placement is the least-squares fit of the same pairs the
gate sees ~0 residuals ("true case"); it rejects degenerate/nan anchor sets (n<3, no radial spread) and a
claimed placement inconsistent with its anchors. The real check on the auto fits is the human's 18/20
sample - the report lists every auto doc's median for that.

`implied = abs(float(a)) * k` but `a` from plan_fit.similarity is COMPLEX (pipeline/plan_fit.py

## 2026-10-11 203a DECISION: session 4d - the two pending fit/batch_us.py fixes from 4c are in: the scale cross-check uses the complex magnitude, and the feature-presence check lands; the 5-pick pilot now routes all four fabrication classes to items and pyramid (the one real fit) stays auto
4c's two pending items, implemented in fit/batch_us.py (the task's only code file; the checkout
elsewhere is untouched, and the pilot writes nothing):
1. BUG FIX: the scale cross-check was `implied = abs(float(a)) * k` but `a` from
   plan_fit.similarity is complex (scale + rotation). numpy's float() discards the imaginary part
   (ComplexWarning), so for a rotated fit implied = |s*cos(theta)|*k - measured on a real hand
   fit (mound-bottom) rotated 60 deg: old 0.5243 vs true 1.0597 m/px, a 2.02x ratio that would
   misfire "not trusted" on a TRUE answer. Now `implied = abs(a) * k` (the magnitude IS the
   scale): the same rotated fit gives exactly ratio 1.000, no misfire. The NaN guard is unchanged.
2. FEATURE-PRESENCE CHECK (the 4c decision, now code): new `_feature_present(site, pts_ll,
   gpath)` after _parse_answer. Grayscale array of the site's own ground image (PIL "L" /255);
   each answer ground point scored by the std of a 24 m box (R=12 px at 1 m/px, centre clamped
   to [R, W-R-1], the inverse of _ground_lonlat through the site corners); null = 400 boxes at
   np.random.default_rng(20261011) (distinct from the report SEED 20261010); pass iff >= half
   the points score >= the null median; ANY read failure -> (True, None) (no evidence never
   blocks; the gate and the human sample are downstream). Wired into the llm_model closure after

## 2026-10-11 203b DECISION: the hand-fitted-sites test went state-aware after the run made two of its pinned plans into pre-docs

The one test that failed after the working run:
test_hand_fitted_sites_get_items_for_their_other_pictures. Session 2 wrote its expectations
for the PRE-run tree: old-sarum's pinned set was its 3 fresh commons rows, but the run made
2 of them (c_041083ec68b532f8, c_ff62c9585a92b375) automatic docs, so the test's recorded run
skips them as pre-docs (never re-fitted, no entry) and the item gained no entry for them
("Extra items in the right set"). Avebury was unaffected (its 5 fresh rows all stayed item
entries, replaced in place). Fix, in my own test file only (no loop change - the skip rule is
203a's correct behaviour): pinned = short-list ∩ fresh (fresh = candidates minus pre_docs,
re-read from the tree at test time); the expected item candidate set = the live item's
candidates (a working run may have left one) ∪ fresh (exact equality, not a superset); the
lead assertion now checks the post-run invariant (exactly one file, named after
candidates[0].plan) instead of "first fresh candidate in file order"; resolved is compared
against the live item's (write-once, never set by the batch). The form is correct before AND
after any run, and under plans.json growth or 212's re-coverage run (the live item's entries
merge in, the fresh ones append). PITFALLS entry filed (recorded-answer batch tests are
state-dependent on the tree).

## 2026-10-11 204 DECISION: cat_chain fixed for the current MediaWiki (prop=categories, fail-loud on warnings) + 60-fetch cap + CHAINS table - 56 walks launched
The first `--chain` probe of the long run (Ghent / Brussels / Luxembourg City) exposed a broken walker: `cat_chain`
fetched a category's parents with `action=query&prop=categoryinfo&cicategories=1&ciclimit=500`, but the current
MediaWiki API does not recognize those parameters (response carries `warnings.main.*: "Unrecognized parameters:
cicategories, ciclimit."` - and `commons.get` returns the body without surfacing the warning). So every walk saw
ZERO parents and silently "failed" in ~1 s per town (even Ghent, which the 2026-10-10 prep measured as holding at
4 hops). Two fixes in fit/src_van_deventer.py (my own file):
- **`prop=categories` + `cllimit=500`** for a category page's CONTAINING categories (verified live: Ghent's van

    hits = [t for t in rows if k in t and t not in used]
    if not hits:
        problems.append(f"rule matches nothing: {k}")
    for t in hits:
        if t in used:
            problems.append(f"double-assigned: {t!r} by rule {k!r}")
        used.add(t)
        inv.append((t, rows[t]["w"], rows[t]["h"], v, rs))
for t in rows:
    if t not in used:
        problems.append(f"UNMATCHED: {t}")

print("verdict counts:", dict(vc), "total:", len(inv))
for p in problems:
    print("PROBLEM:", p)
for t, w, h, v, rs in inv:
    if v == "staged" and max(w, h) < 1000: problems.append(f"staged but small: {t}")
    if v == "drop: too small" and max(w, h) >= 1000: problems.append(f"too-small but big: {t}")
if problems:
    raise SystemExit(1)

def q(s):
    return repr(s)
lines = [f"    ({q(t)}, {w}, {h}, {q(v)}, {q(rs)})," for t, w, h, v, rs in sorted(inv)]
block = "INVENTORY = [\n" + "\n".join(lines) + "\n]\n"

assert src.count(old) == 1
src = src.replace(old, block)
old_doc = "(an empty INVENTORY only lists - the first run builds it)"
assert src.count(old_doc) == 1
src = src.replace(old_doc, "(the committed 132-row table; a renamed, re-filed or replaced file fails loud)")
open(path, "w").write(src)

### 2026-10-11 206 DECISION: the p.212 plan is printed NORTH-UP (page top = north), not north-left as the arrow suggests; the surviving ring is the C11 motte
    Two findings from measuring the fetched page against the ground (details in the task hand-over): (1) The book's p.212 drawing (pentagon, five towers, hall, dashed building, gate) sits in the page's top-left quadrant (bbox ~(10,0)-(425,425) of the 839x840 frame). The only clear surviving ring on the LiDAR/aerial is a ~40 m ditched mound at (E +0..+11 m, N -46..-48 m) from the catalog point - the size and ditch match the C11 MOTTE (Gatehouse 212: 40x20 m hexagonal mound, 25 m ditch), not a 12 m castle tower. With the three reliable anchors (plan hall -> the bright building cluster NW of centre; plan dashed building -> the speck W; plan T4 (bottom horseshoe) -> the motte) the solved similarity under the printed orientation (page left = N, per the arrow) is rotated ~90 deg off the ground, while under north-up it comes out with rotation ~0 deg, scale ~0.41 m/px, the pentagon's south corner due south on the motte and the hall on the NW building: the plan is a normal north-up map and the printed left-pointing arrow is 90 deg off (or marks something else - /tmp/arrow_crop.jpg, 4x zoom of page (170,235)-(345,290), to be re-read; /tmp may be gone). ### 2026-10-11 206 DECISION: the book's own V2 text identifies the plate's castle (OQ-3 resolved); the plan is the 1600 Randle Holme drawing, a pentagon with SIX towers, five drawn
    Re-downloaded the V2 OCR (archive.org castlesofengland02mack: hocr searchtext/pageindex + page_numbers; the page_numbers file is format v2 {identifier, format-version, confidence, pages:[{leafNum, pageNumber}]} and pageindex rows are [leafStart, leafEnd, textStart, textEnd] - the prep's "leaf->printed map" guess was wrong). The Shotwick chapter (printed p.180, running head CHESHIRE 181 on the continuation page; next chapter STOCKPORT) says: the plan is "a drawing and plan of this fortress by Kendle [Randle] Holme, as it appeared then, in a ruinous condition. Its trace was a pentagon strengthened by six towers, one of which, according to Camden, was five storeys high", and of the 1897 remains: "those seen at present consisting merely of a large mound, supported by a huge earthwork of crescent form, and two deep entrenchments on the land side". The index reads "Shotlack, ii. 179, Shotwick, ii. 180". So the p.212 plate (leaf 212 = printed 164; the Lancaster plate leaf 231 = printed 183, 19 pages on) is a plan of Shotwick drawn from Holme's c.1600 depiction of the ruined fortress - which explains the five (of six) towers, the thick bank, and why the modern ground only carries the motte + crescent + entrenchments. This is the backbone of docs/lead_mackenzie.md section 3 (evidence chain a-f) and of the fit's expectations.

Commands: --fetch (resumable, idempotent, 4 workers; missing/empty book dir raises a SystemExit naming ask_human 001), --status (offline: leaves, triage progress, LLM ports), --triage A|F|B (delegates to the unmodified books.cmd_triage_*). # Task 212 cover-final

## 2026-10-12 212 DECISION: fit/cover.py designed - six phases on an injectable root, the live run later
The task's loop, search and sync become one module, fit/cover.py (new; its tests tests/test_cover.py).
Design settled after reading site_done.py, matchfit.py, batch_us.run_sites, review.upsert_item/export,
commons (search/files_of/keep/info/thumbs/classify), fit/evidence.record, plan_fit, export_plans and
serve.after_write. Phases (each takes root, so a test drives them on a temp tree; a CLI runs them in
order, `all`, with --root and --working/--model-json like site_done):

1. fetch(root): local copies before export_plans (the lead's second point). Files with a `thumb`
   missing their local jpg: fetch the 1280 thumb (commons.thumbs' behaviour: .part->rename, 1/s pace,
   resumable - re-implemented here with a root parameter; commons.thumbs itself is bound to the
   checkout's module-level RAW/OUT). Files with only a `url` (the ORL/Limes rows, 54): commons.info(
   [title]) gives the 1280 thumburl (imageinfo iiurlwidth=1280) - fetch that; fall back to the raw
   url (utm-stripped) when info has no thumb. Then regenerate web/data/plans.json with
   export_plans.main() (in-process; its ROOT/BOOKS and commons' OUT/RAW are module constants - a
   temp-tree test monkeypatches them, that is setup, not product behaviour). Measured on the synced
   tree (main a858f48): 131 classified rows missing a local copy (ALL meet the plans threshold
   p_photo<0.5 and max(p_plan,p_birdseye)>=0.3, none in plans yet -> plans.json grows 1168 -> ~1299,
   matching the lead's Mac 1296); 401 thumb rows missing locally; 54 url-only rows (1 has a copy).
   The 211 rows are ALREADY classified (all 930 classified rows are in files.jsonl) - no classifier
   needed for them, only copies.
2. search(root): for every BUILT site with no fit (no doc and drawings 0 - recomputed after phase 1,
   so sites that just gained candidates drop out of the set) and no plans.json candidate: with a qid -
   (a) its P373 category via commons.wd_claims, files with commons.files_of(cat, depth=1); (b) P180 -
   evidence.fetch_page_ids + fetch_file_entities on every title gathered so far, keep the ones whose
   MediaInfo depicts the qid (the proven path, not a new API); (c) the title search
   commons.search(name) (its 3 full-text queries). Without a qid: (c) only, and the record says so.
   Keep with commons.keep (1925 cut-off, no regex); dedupe against files.jsonl titles. Per site the
   SEARCH RECORD names exactly what ran: the category (name or "none"), the file counts, the qid
   queried for P180 (or "no qid"), the 3 title queries, the date, and any route that failed (a
   429/timeout is recorded, not hidden - the record must be true).
3. stage(root): newly found files -> files.jsonl (harvest row shape + qid + by:"212") + local copy
   (phase 1's fetcher) + classified.jsonl via an INJECTABLE classifier (default the clef batch,
   commons.classify's questions) + the 200 evidence field via evidence.record(files, books, live,
   only=new sites) (live in the working phase; a stub in tests) + export_plans again (growth-only).
4. loop(root, model=None): the normal loop, and the FIT IS THE MATCHER (see next entry). For every
   built site that still has no fit, run site_done.main([sid, --root root]) in-process WITHOUT
   --working: matchfit.run (ELoFTR 8091; RoMa 8092 is down on this VM and skipped automatically)
   writes a doc (fitter:"matcher") for every picture it is sure of, including ones already in a
   review item (a confident matcher fit resolves the item); the rest get batch_us.run_sites'
   upsert ("no model answer" when model=None) into the item; a site with zero candidates gets the
   batch's no_picture item, which phase 5 re-records with the exact searched string. site_done
   already syncs each new doc (line check: agent docs get the matcher's spread guard, not the
   batch-model ladder clause), refreshes drawings, and scopes the review export to the site.
   --working (the vision model, 301) is NEVER passed by 212: it invented points and must not place.
5. nopicture(root): every search-set site that ends with no candidates and no fit gets
   review.upsert_item(root, sid, [], no_picture={searched: <exact record>, at}) - entries=[] + a
   dict keeps any existing candidates (verified in upsert_item: the dict branch wins; candidates are
   merged, never cleared) and rewrites the batch's generic "plans.json (N rows, ...)" searched string
   with the exact one. A site whose search routes all failed gets the item too, with the failures
   recorded - box 6's invariant (every built site: drawings >= 1 OR an open item) holds even when
   the network lies.
6. sync(root) + export(root) + report(root): sync = the page-facing sync (box 3), a plan_fit sweep
   over EVERY doc but per-doc proof: plan_fit.main's own loop only catches SystemExit per doc (the
   serve worker catches the WHOLE sweep and gives up, serve.py ~line 261-273), so cover owns the
   loop and imports plan_fit's primitives (who_placed, is_done, build, prune, NO_PROVENANCE): per
   doc, hand -> build with no check; agent -> build; unmarked auto -> stamp by:agent then build;
   no provenance -> refuse (item entry); ANY other exception -> record the failure, continue, and
   upsert that site's item with the build-failure reason (so the invariant holds when an overlay
   cannot be built). prune at the end (the deleted docs' overlays). export = review.export(root)
   full (box 4, the one and only writer of web/data/review.json). report = docs/batch.md (box 5) in
   batch_us.write_report's shape but FINAL over all built sites: counts per outcome (fit hand = the
   golden 21, fit automatic = every by:agent doc (batch + matcher + line-saved), human-saved =
   by:hand docs outside the golden 21, review item, no picture found), the 20-sample of
   automatically accepted fits drawn from the WHOLE auto-doc union with 212's OWN recorded seed
   SEED_212 = 20261012 (batch 20261010, null 20261011 - the date convention) and page URL + gate
   score per pick, and the no-picture list with each site's exact searched record.

Tests (tests/test_cover.py, no network, port 0): temp tree (conftest pattern: web/ + data/ copied,
per-site web dirs, stand-in pictures PIL-drawn to the doc's size) seeded with a matcher doc, a
golden hand doc, an unmarked auto doc, a no-provenance doc and a bad-commons doc; monkeypatched
(setup, not product): the commons/evidence network getters (recorded titles/metadata), the
classifier (recorded p_*), matchfit.reachable/run (a recorded confident fit and the unreachable
case), export_plans' ROOT/BOOKS and commons' OUT/RAW (the temp root). Drive the phases in-process,
then check through the SERVED page (the served fixture, port 0): every built site in the served
sites.json has drawings >= 1 or is in the served review.json open list (box 6, the GOAL point 1 in
full); the 000 golden test re-runs unchanged (the 21 hand docs and 19 site.json stay byte-identical -
verified separately with sha256sum -c after every live run); the docs/batch.md sample equals
random.Random(SEED_212).sample(sorted auto-doc ids, 20) recomputed in the test (fixed, reproducible
- the human's 18/20 check depends on it). State-aware per the 203b pitfall: the test computes its
expected sets from the temp tree's live docs/items, never from pinned counts (agent c's 302a/304/306
drift the live store in parallel).

## 2026-10-12 212 DECISION: the loop's fit is the matcher, never the vision model (the lead, ef84a05)
The lead note (commit ef84a05, merged into this branch 2026-10-12) steers the task: the fit in 212's
loop is the MATCHER via tools/site_done.py, never a vision-model fit. Rationale recorded by the
lead: the vision-model batch fit invented its points (301) and must not place anything; an unsure
matcher result goes to the review item, as site_done already does. Evidence on this VM (measured
this session): ELoFTR on 127.0.0.1:8091 answers /health (matchanything_eloftr on the RTX 5060 Ti)
so matchfit.reachable() is TRUE here - the matcher pass will actually run in the working phase;
RoMa on 8092 does not answer (matchfit.run skips its second pass when it is down, by design).
Consequently 212's loop runs site_done WITHOUT --working and WITHOUT --model-json (model=None):
the matcher places what it is sure of (>= 10 inliers, rotation within 30 deg, spread guard -
matchfit.judge); the rest land in the review item as "no model answer" (batch_us.run_sites'
upsert, the path site_done already uses). This supersedes the iteration-200 hand-over plan that
had the loop on batch_us.llm_model (the AI-box LLM on 8081 does answer, but it is the 301 fabricator
and the lead forbids it for placement). The vision model may still be used nowhere in 212: not for
placement, and not as a classifier substitute without a human decision (see next entry).

## 2026-10-12 212 DECISION: fetch-before-export measured; clef unreachable from this VM, so the classifier is injectable and its use in the working phase is a human decision

## 2026-10-11 213 DECISION: the prep's Imola "centre 44.245 N, 12.367 E / bad P625 53 km NW" was wrong - that point is Cervia; P625 is the correct city point
The prep notes placed Imola's old town at 44.245 N, 12.367 E and, seeing Q50195's P625 (44.353, 11.715) far
from it, called the P625 "bad, ~53 km NW of the town". Verified live (2026-10-11): the prep point is CERVIA
on the Ravenna coast (~50 km SE of Imola); the real city is at 44.353 N, 11.715 E, where THREE independent
sources agree: the enwiki infobox (44°21'11"N 11°42'53"E), Wikidata P625, and the OSM town node (with the F1
circuit beside it and the Santerno - "Fiume Santerno" at 44.3606/11.7104 - running through the urban area).
So the "53 km trap" was the distance between two wrong values. Consequences: (a) the site point is the
walled town's centre, 11.7112/44.3535 (Piazza del Duomo, OSM) - the centre of the sheet's circular view, not
the modern city point; (b) the prep's "Savena crossing" was a second error - the drawing's river is the
Santerno, which Leonardo labels "Sant'Arno" (mirror script, read off the sheet); the view is south-up per
the literature; (c) the evidence story changes: for Imola the live record route resolves the RIGHT QID (the
hand record still stands to pin the walled centre, deterministic and offline); the name-search trap that is
REAL and documented is Venice (first hit with P625 = Q773853 Venice, California, 9891 km). Side note: OSM's
comune boundary for Imola is mis-drawn (Nominatim displays the urban area as "Imola, Nuovo Circondario
Imolese", and the admin relation's centre sits 8 km north of the city) - a reason never to geocode Imola
from OSM/Nominatim. The PITFALLS entry "Q50195 (Imola) carries a bad P625..." must be corrected accordingly

## 2026-10-12 219 DECISION: 302c no longer blocks - the lead dropped 302c/302d in main d39ead8

commit d39ead8 (main, 2026-10-12) dropped 302c/302d as superseded by the matcher fit and set 219's
Depends line to `none`. 302c never made its design changes to plan_fit.py (its own hand-over:
investigation only, no code), so nothing from it collides with 219's edit; plan_fit.py is
byte-identical between my branch and main (merge-base e2ca3d9; main's only commit since is d39ead8,
task files + journals only). Proceeded on this branch without waiting.

## 2026-10-12 219 DECISION: year-once rule = drop the label parenthesis whenever the title carries any 4-digit year
The task's two sentences ("drop the label's parenthesis when the title already contains that year"
vs "only a title without a year shows the label (or 'undated')") diverge for the 3 docs whose
label-year differs from the title-year (argentoratum 1831/1836, bethlehem 1881/1882, mound-bottom
1923/1924). Implemented the stricter, unambiguous one: the parenthesis appears ONLY for a yearless
title (label or "undated"); a titled year always drops it. The label is not lost from the page: it
stays in the entry's `scale` field. The year check reuses the same 4-digit pattern as the entry's
sort year (_year4) so the two can never disagree; non-4-digit numbers ("116", "0154", 5-digit ids,
"17th century") are not years, so "(1750-1900)"-style labels still show under yearless titles.

## 2026-10-12 219 DECISION: refactor source_line extraction is byte-identical for all 133 store docs
Extracted the citation + who/how clause from build() into pure source_line(doc, n, m, who) and the
year regex into _year4 (committed 4b93f5c). Proof: a throwaway script evaluated the old inline
expressions (copied verbatim from HEAD) and the new function for every doc in data/db/platefits
(133) with m from similarity(doc['pairs']) unscaled - 0 mismatches. The least-squares similarity is
scale-equivariant (scaling all u,v by the picture's fs scales a back by 1/fs, leaving the ground
residuals the same), so m and corners do not depend on which image size stands in for the picture;
this is why the hermetic test can build with a stand-in image of the doc's own frame size (fs=1)
and still pin the exact how-clause.

## 2026-10-12 219 DECISION: re-bake = plan_fit.build per stale entry, then restore sites.json byte-for-byte
The one-off re-bake (14 built year-titled commons depictions + shotwick, which had never been
built in this checkout) ran the product's own path: plan_fit.build(doc) per doc, root = this
checkout. Contrary to the previous hand-over's expectation, every big picture was already
cached in data/raw/commons/big/ -> zero downloads. Proof that "only the string changes": for
all 14 the rebuilt entry equals the stored one in every field except source; a second
identical run is byte-stable (the fixed state is a fixed point); shotwick's rebuilt entry
matches agent a's built entry (corners, fit, year, label, scale, coverage, kind, file, ink)
with only the source fixed. Each build's trailing build_site.set_drawings refreshed
web/data/sites.json (tracked, in 306's Touches) - the committed bookkeeping was stale (5
sites: drawings 0 despite built plans, bethlehem 0->12) - and I restored the committed
bytes: a gitignored build does not change committed bookkeeping (agent a's checkout follows
the same convention); the product refreshes the file on its own next time. The naive
verification check ("(label)" in source) false-positives on 3 of the 15 (avaricum, bolsover,
castle-rising: the label string occurs inside the title itself) - the structural test is
source.split(", Wikimedia Commons:")[0] == title (PITFALLS).

## 2026-10-11 301 DECISION: lead redirect - Stonehenge is not done first; its 7 batch fits are all fabricated frame-to-box identity maps, and the gate passed them by construction
The lead (mid-session, 2026-10-11): before Argentoratum, check each of Stonehenge's 7 synced drawings; anything visibly off goes to the review queue with the reason; find why the gate passed the Rijksmuseum plan (16.7 m, 2-3x too big, off-centre) and make the LINE catch it, with a test; correct the false sentence in docs/site_flow.md; then Argentoratum.
Root cause (verified this session): all 7 stonehenge auto docs (c_0226 23.2 m, c_098c 7.4 m, c_20f9 44.1 m, c_6933 26.8 m, c_83b4 16.7 m, c_897a 38.0 m, c_f838 0.0 m) are the model's documented fabrication class (batch_us.llm_model docstring, pilots 4a/4c: "internally perfect regular patterns (identity maps, corner-to-corner, diagonal ladders)"): regular ladders of round page-px coordinates (u 200-1080 step ~200-400, v 150-1200 step ~100-200) mapped to regular ground ladders (points on shared lon/lat lines 100-450 m from the site centre; 4 of the 7 have one anchor within ~1 m of the site's NOMINAL centre - the catalog coordinate, not a feature), implied scale 0.80-1.07 m/px = box width / page px (the model treated the page frame as the 1000x1000 m site box). Why the gate passed it: run_sites never asks the model for a placement - it SOLVES the similarity from the model's own pairs and the gate scores that least-squares fit against the same points, so the residuals are only the ladder's ~20-25% anisotropy + jitter (med 0-44 m < 45, slope_o 0.02-0.12 < 0.145, no radial pattern) -> ACCEPT. That is gate.md section 7's registered limit verbatim ("a consistent global error passes"; the gate does not re-verify the anchors are the right features) - the gate did its registered job. The batch's three pre-gate counterchecks all pass BY CONSTRUCTION on this class: the stated-scale cross-check compares the model's stated scale with its own ladder's implied scale (they agree by construction), and _feature_present passes because ladder points scattered over structureless Salisbury Plain sit at/above the 400-point null median (the next-door candidate c_ffb3d drew the 25% verdict). All 7 verified visually (composites over relief.jpg, /tmp/stonehenge_overlay_check.png): none sits on the sarsens - c_83b4 is 2-3x too big AND ~70 m off-centre (the lead's exact description), the other six likewise off in scale and/or position. Consequence the lead accepts: all 13 of Stonehenge's candidates end in the review item (human's drag is the last word) and the site shows 0 drawings until a human fits at least one.

## 2026-10-11 301 DECISION: the line's fix - a fabrication-pattern check (2D lattice / 1D ladder / frame-identity) before sync; pattern docs go to the review item with the reason, never to the map
Chosen over extending the frozen gate (that would void the gate.md registration and test_gate pins its constants) and over re-running the batch (the batch's pre-gate checks are exactly what passed by construction; the line is the last gate before the map and re-validates each site's docs on its turn - no batch-wide re-run needed). Shape (detailed in the task hand-over): a new pure function in pipeline/plan_fit.py, `fabrication_pattern(pairs, crop, size, box) -> None | reason`, three conditions any one of which fires: (a) 2D lattice (>=3 distinct u AND >=3 distinct v, consecutive gaps near-arithmetic on both axes, >=4 anchors) - fires on c_098c, c_83b4; (b) 1D ladder (>=3 anchors collinear with near-arithmetic spacing) - fires on c_0226; (c) frame-identity (the solved similarity maps the crop frame onto the site box: centre within 25% of the box side per axis, size ratio per axis in [0.7, 1.4]) - fires on c_20f9, c_6933, c_897a, c_f838. site_done._sync runs it before any download; on a hit: no build, prune any existing overlay (plan_fit.prune), upsert a review-item candidate carrying the doc's pairs + gate score + the pattern reason, recompute the entry and republish the queue. Tolerances must be validated to fire on all 7 stonehenge docs and on NONE of the 20 hand-fit docs (the golden reference). Then run the line on stonehenge (no model needed: all 13 candidates covered -> no batch run, no network: pattern docs are rejected before any fetch), fix site_flow.md + replace stonehenge.png, then argentoratum.

### 2026-10-11 301 DECISION: the line's fabrication check = standalone grid-roundness plus 2D-lattice and 1D-ladder clauses on the doc's page-px pairs; frame-identity dropped, so the function takes pairs only
Chosen of the two options the previous hand-over left open: standalone grid-roundness as the primary clause (its own recommendation: a strict gate that over-refuses is fine, the human's drag is the last word, and it fires on ALL 8 argentoratum docs, not just the 5 the frame-identity+round variant caught). Frame-identity is dropped entirely: it fires on 4 legitimate hand maps (avebury/bergues/calleva/camp-d "the drawing covers the site box"; rotation cannot separate them, tested last session) and adds no coverage (roundness already fires all 15 targets). With frame-identity gone, crop/size/box are dead params, so the implemented signature is fabrication_pattern(pairs) in pipeline/plan_fit.py (pure numpy, no download; runs on the doc's stored pairs in the picture's size frame, before any fetch). (b) is kept because it is not redundant: pontefract c_3213 (22% round) is a 1D ladder - the union of the three clauses fires on EVERY batch auto doc in the repo (110/110 in data/db/platefits), not just the 15 targets.

## 2026-10-11 302a DECISION: placement->similarity geometry verified; b convention is complex(u0c, -v0c) (MINUS-v) - the session-3 script's +v0c was an 860 m near-miss
Session 4: re-ran the session-3 verification script (kept in the iter-0075 log) and found it had a SECOND bug beyond the noted broadcast fix: it applied M to [du, dv] instead of the autofit convention d = [du, -(v - v0)]. With both fixed (d = [u-u0c, -(v-v0c)], en = d @ M.T + t; lon/lat = aw.to_lonlat(cx + e/k, cy + n/k), k = 1/aw.ground_scale(lat)):
- plan_fit.similarity recovers a = k*s*exp(i*rot) to relative error 7e-6 (= the 1 dp px / 7 dp lon-lat rounding limit of the synthetic pairs), residuals 1.4-4.6 mm; fit_gate.gate accepts (med 3 mm).
- **b = (cx + k*tE) + i(cy + k*tN) - a*complex(u0c, -v0c)** — the minus-v form. The session-3 script used complex(u0c, +v0c) and reported a relative error of 1.3e-4, which looked fine only because |b| ~ 6.6e6 m absorbs the 860 m disagreement. Cross-checked both ways: the solved b matches zc - a*complex(u0,-v0) to the rounding limit, and re-fitting propose._anchor_pairs' 5 pairs recovers that anchor's a and b exactly (a = (m_per_px/ground_scale)*e^(i*rot), b = zc - a*complex(u0, -v0)).
fit/inkfit.py's placement_of and map_pairs must use the minus-v w0 and the flipped-v d; the rest of the design stands as recorded in the task file.

  the margin clears the threshold - that outcome gets reported plainly, not papered over.

<!-- task 302c -->
# Task 302c decision-wiring

## 2026-10-12 302c DECISION: the confidence threshold is 0.15, set on the 302b held-out table (box 1) - the null margin only rations the pass rate; it is not an accuracy guarantee
First session on 302c (iteration 84): investigation and design only, no code written (the context
limit hit before the first edit). The value and the design, frozen for the next session:
- Threshold CONF_THRESHOLD = 0.15 on the search-matched-null margin (confidence = objective_fit
  - max(scramble, shifted) as fit/inkfit.py already computes). Rationale from the 302b table
  (docs/site_flow.md "Measured one-shot"): sorted margins run -0.5150..+0.1871 and do NOT
  separate good from bad fits (worst calleva +0.1070/2203.6 m sits above castle-rising +0.0806
  and old-sarum-book +0.0693). A threshold > 0 passes 11 docs, > 0.05 passes 6, > 0.10 passes 2
  (badbury AND the worst, calleva); only a threshold in (0.1070, 0.1871] passes exactly one
  document - badbury, the best (264.5 m, 17% of the site's size). 0.15 is mid-interval: 0.043 of
  room above calleva's rounded 0.1070 and 0.037 below badbury's 0.1871, robust to small DEM/OSM
  drift between the held-out run and a re-run. A future change to the value is a method change:
  it must be labelled and re-measured, never a silent fix.
- Decision (applied in fit/inkfit.py, additive): confident iff the fit produced reportable pairs
  AND the frozen gate accepted them (verdict == fit_gate.ACCEPT) AND fabrication_pattern is
  silent AND the null ran AND margin >= 0.15. Everything else is unsure with a
  human-readable reason (the existing no-fit reasons are already human-readable; new: a gate
  refusal names the median residual; a below-threshold margin names the margin, the fit and
  null objectives and which null won - per the 302a hand-over note). Confident -> automatic
  platefit document (auto: true, fitter: "ink", the gate's score); unsure -> the site's review
  item with the reason and the best starting pairs, never to the map.
- New result fields are "confident" (bool) and "unsure_reason" (str|None). The "reason" field
  keeps its exact meaning (None on the success path): inkfit_heldout.measure() stores r["reason"]
  into the frozen one-shot checkpoint (data/inkfit/heldout/results.json), so routing the margin
  message through "reason" would corrupt the checkpoint if measure were ever re-run. "confident"/
  "unsure_reason" are new keys measure() does not store, so the checkpoint and the verbatim table
  stay untouched (verify: `fit/inkfit_heldout.py table` byte-identical to the committed section).
- Task file: Touches extended to docs/site_flow.md (the decision paragraph goes next to the
table), data/inkfit/ (the committed test-site relief npz seeds under data/inkfit/relief/, the
committed real-plate copies under data/inkfit/plates/) and tests/test_site_done.py (the
no-model CLI message of site_done changes wording, and that test asserts the line verbatim).
Next session: implement box 1 exactly as the hand-over spells it (the decide() contract, the
site_flow.md paragraph text, the verification list incl. applying decide() to the 21 checkpoint
entries -> exactly badbury confident), then box 2 (site_done wiring), 3 (plan_fit.build how
string) and 4 (tests/test_inkfit.py + the committed seeds; badbury = confident e2e, calleva =
unsure e2e).

## 2026-10-12 304 DECISION: re-read passes on the +theta sign convention (no flip); panel_pieces fixed to mirror template_pieces' piece selection so the scramble draws land exactly as 302b's

Session 3. The file was already committed by the driver (3b4c2b2 "[driver] uncommitted
work after iteration 86"); the import check passed clean (no breakage to fix). The
three Re-read items were re-verified with fresh eyes against the source:

1. **Sign convention (CRITICAL item) - passes, no flip.**
   `propose._anchor_pairs` is `z = (m_per_px/k) * e^{i theta} * (w - wc) + zc` with
   `w = u - i v` (page coords, v down) and `z` Mercator (imag = north). A visual
   (on-screen) counterclockwise rotation by phi multiplies the `w = x - i y` frame by
   **+e^{i phi}** (verified: at 90 deg the up vector (0,-1) goes to left (-1,0), which is
   CCW on screen and +i in the w frame). A drawn plan whose north arrow is theta deg
   CLOCKWISE of page-up has the 302b anchor factor e^{i theta}; rotating the panel image
   by **+theta** (PIL `rotate(+deg)` is counterclockwise on screen) brings it north-up.
   So `_match_theta`'s `rotate_image(panel, +theta)` and `rotated_panel_map`'s
   `R = [[c, s], [-s, c]]` (the visual-CCW matrix in x-right/y-down) are both correct,
   and the composition `a_s * a_r * e^{i theta} * fs` is exactly the anchor form
   `(m/k) e^{i theta}`. The synthetic test must still lock this (see hand-over).
2. **Frame separation in `composite_placement` - passes.** The similarity (a, b) is fit
   on the four FULL-FRAME (doc size frame) corners; the reported panel corners are the
   CROP-box corners (size units, `_panel_crop`: map_box fractions * size, or (0,0,w,h)
   full frame) pushed through that same similarity. The composition of the three
   stage maps is an exact similarity in the w frame, so the full-frame fit is valid at

   a call one fine step (2 deg) away from the true rotation still resolves and returns all

   rotation's score and the sweep's first-max rule could land on 358/2 instead of 0. Fix

   by up to 0.6 px per degree of angular error, seeded per (theta, i) - deterministic and
   repeat-call-stable, mimicking a matcher whose match QUALITY degrades with rotation. The
   resulting score landscape is strictly ordered: delta 0 ~0.52 > delta 2 ~0.48 >> delta
   4-15 ~0.15-0.19 ~ junk-only ~0.15. The sweep is now deterministic: theta_d=0 -> 0, theta
   _d=6 -> 6, unique maxima in both cases (the fine-0 duplicate payload ties the coarse 0
   and the strict > keeps the first).

- SHELL/QUirks hit this session (for the record): (a) `python3 -c "...$d_fit.json"` in bash expands `$d_fit` as ONE variable name (underscore is a valid name char) - use `${d}_fit.json`; (b) PIL is only in the project .venv, not system python3; (c) `for ... in range(*range)` shadowing the builtin `range` raises `TypeError: range() argument after * must be an iterable`; (d) tuple-of-tuple lists do NOT flatten when unpacked (`L, y0, y1, x = cand[0]` where cand[0] = ((L,s,e), x) fails with "expected 4, got 2"); (e) scale bars on these plates are often SEGMENTED (black/white divisions) - the longest single dark run is one segment, you must merge all runs in the bar row band; the 2x-zoomed bar crop (read the image) is the most reliable measurement method.

The iteration-108 session investigated the original 307a (the namesake place check) and

work). It wrote the re-split record and the full 309 spec but never wrote the DECISIONS

- Place-check rule set: decide from KNOWN places only - a mismatch only when a known
  caption place contradicts the site's (a different county within one country, a
different country, or resolved coordinates far outside the site's region); an unknown
place never mismatches (fail open - necessary because 52 queue candidates carry noisy
recorded conflicts that are mostly title words, not places); a place that contains the
site (a country-level word, the site's own county/name) is not a mismatch; re-verify
recorded verdicts offline (the evidence-check pattern: a recorded mismatch whose stored
coordinates no longer contradict is flagged, not silently kept).

# Task 307bb move-it

## 2026-10-12 307bb DECISION: the placement gestures live in fitkit.js by reassigning refit (no index.html footprint, no new map listeners) - designed in full, not yet coded
Investigation-only session: 307ba is done (suite 75+1, re-claimed at c5250a4 sync), so
307bb's start condition is met. No code written; the full implementation design (function
by function) is in 307bb's hand-over. Key decisions, all verified against the sources:

- **MapLibre 5.6.0 binds ALL gesture listeners on the canvas container, not the canvas**
  (web/vendor/maplibre-gl-5.6.0.js, readable UMD: mousedown/mousemove/mouseup/dblclick/
  click/wheel{passive:false} on getCanvasContainer(), mousemove{capture}/mouseup on
  document). Consequence: fitkit's gesture listeners go on the container; with
  dragPan/scrollZoom/touchZoomRotate/doubleClickZoom/boxZoom disabled while placed, the
  dispatcher (`if(!c.isEnabled())continue;`) skips them and none preventDefaults (the
  scrollZoom handler returns before its e.preventDefault() when disabled) - a
  later-registered container listener receives the events, so wheel/drag can own the mouse
  without fighting the map.
- **The 3px/4px disjointness is real, not assumed:** the always-enabled user-event handler
  records _mousedownPos on every mousedown and fires the map 'click' only when the
  mousedown->click distance is < clickTolerance (3 px, the page's default). Our move
  engages at >4 px, so a pinning click and a moving drag cannot both fire; we null
  P.pending the moment a move engages (a drag is not a pin).
- **Anchor refinement hooks through a wrapped refit, not a map listener:** the page's own
  map-click (pin), undo, clear and marker-dragend handlers all call the bare refit() - the
  global - so `refit = wrapper` sees every pair-count change: n grew -> push the pre-pin
  anchor(s) on P.anchorStack, refine the anchor by simFit over all pairs (view mode too:
  the anchor stays a similarity; verified algebraically simFit's a,b equal the re-emitted
  similarity's a,z0, so over the exact five it recovers the anchor to fp rounding),
  re-emit the five in place (mutate lon/lat, keep the objects - the marker dragend
  closures hold them), rebuild markers via the page's addPairMarker (push one at a time
  for 1..n labels); n shrank -> pop the stack (clear -> the anchor before the first pin;
  undo below the five-re-emit floor with an empty stack leaves the anchor untouched: the
  placement is inviolable). A drag gesture does NOT absorb the fit first (a move must not
  change mpx/rot); wheel/rotate do (so a previously dragged corner is absorbed into the
  anchor before the transform).
- **Gestures transform the anchor:** drag = centre += ground delta (unproject at both
  pointer points, exact at any zoom, fly-to-tolerant); wheel = mpx *= exp(-deltaY*0.0015)
  (the page canvas's own factor: wheel-up grows); shift+wheel = rot += deltaY*0.01 (1 deg
  per 100-unit notch). Applied rAF-coalesced (headless rAF works on this VM - the 307ba
  probe's fly-to animations ran). The page's fit pane already shows the fit's mpx/rot;
  fitkit additionally overwrites #fithint after each refit with the live anchor readout +
  gesture legend (box 1's "live scale and rotation in the panel").
- **Save needs no new code:** with P.pairs = re-emitted five (+ pins), the page's saveFit
  already writes exactly the doc the box asks for (same page-px frame: 307ba verified
  every current queue entry's served image IS its recorded size, so the row-size frame is
  the image frame). The fitqueue wrapper marks the site done; the one-site line runs as in
  part 2. The headless proof (box 3) pins all of it in pixels.
- **Deactivate placement at the TOP of the openPlan wrapper** (before the inner chain):
  review.js's wrapper pushes RV.pending pairs inside the chain and "Another plan" is
  endFit(false)->startFit->openPlan - a post-chain clear would let either inherit the
  previous placement; the 404-page path (part 3's served tree) still returns at the first
  P.img guard, byte-identical (keep that guard first).

**The bug caught (why the rest of the probe never ran):** web/index.html:342-343 defines `merc = ([lon, lat]) => ...` / `unmerc = ([x, y]) => ...` - they destructure ARRAYS. fitkit's `_fkOnDown` stores `ll: map.unproject(pos)` and `_fkOnMove` computes `b = merc(map.unproject([x, y]))`, but MapLibre 5.6's unproject returns a LngLat OBJECT {lng, lat} - array destructuring of an object yields undefined -> the anchor's lon/lat become NaN on the first drag move (every re-emit after is NaN; the wheel's _fkAbsorb would then poison scale/rotation too). The iter-123 hand-over's design (item 11) contained the same latent bug (`ll: map.unproject(pos)`), so iteration 124's code faithfully reproduces it - this is a DESIGN bug, not a transcription slip. The fix (next session, before any further gesture work): in `_fkOnDown` store `ll: [u.lng, u.lat]` and in `_fkOnMove` compute `b = merc([u.lng, u.lat])` from the unproject result - a one-line-class change, no restructure; then re-run the whole probe end-to-end (the drag/wheel/turn/pin/undo/save/cancel assertions have NOT yet been observed passing).

### 2026-10-12 307bb DECISION: iteration 127 - the probe re-run: all 33 gesture/pin/undo/save-doc checks GREEN; the save mystery solved (the GUARD's dead pipe, not the page) and three probe bugs fixed; remaining: run the server under the venv python (site_done needs numpy), fix the depSel seed shape, allow Esri in the reqfail filter
Ran the iter-126 next step: killed the stale tree server, rebuilt (the fixed fitkit lands in the tree), re-ran the throwaway probe. Run 127 (pre build_tree fix) got 33 [ok] - all seed, drag (the 1.5x bug is gone), wheel, shift+wheel (the rotated-parallelogram claim verified in pixels), pin, undo - then failed at save (S.db null) and crashed on its own `site is not defined` in the run-2 cancel evaluate.

**The save mystery, solved (the biggest finding):** build_tree.py read the GUARD server's stdout pipe only up to the URL line and then EXITS - closing the pipe's read end. Every subsequent `sys.stderr.write` in the server raises BrokenPipeError. serve.py's `log_message` writes on EVERY /api/ request and every non-200 status, and BaseHTTPRequestHandler calls `log_request` INSIDE `send_response` - before the buffered status line is flushed by end_headers. So with the dead pipe, every /api/ response (including /api/db/ping, the page's db handshake) and every 404 died mid-response: the browser saw ERR_EMPTY_RESPONSE, the page's openDb (index.html ~1499) returned null, S.db stayed null, and saveFit returned silently at its first line (`if (!S.db || ...) return;`) - status text untouched, no pageerror, no PUT. 200-static files skip the log and work, which is why the page loaded, the book page loaded, and all placement checks passed. Proven live: with the pipe dead, curl showed /api/db/ping and non-existent /data/ files = "Empty reply from server", while /data/fit_queue.json = 200 OK; the server process had 1 thread (all handler threads dead). Fix (in /tmp/fkverify/build_tree.py only): the server's stdout/stderr go to a FILE (tree.log) - a file has no read end, so nothing blocks, dies, or fills. After the fix, run 127b: ping OK, db:true, the page's own PUT landed, and the doc was written to the tree store with by:hand, size = the loaded image, and pairs EXACTLY the final re-emitted five (the page's own rounding) - box 2's core proven end-to-end in the browser. The committed line_served fixture is unaffected (pytest keeps a reader thread on the pipe for the test's lifetime, and the test PUTs from the test process, never through the page).

**Three probe bugs fixed in /tmp/fkverify/probe.mjs (none are page bugs):**
1. "pin: the anchor was refined" read `pinOut.u0`/`pinOut.v0` - the keys don't exist (u0/v0 are under `pinOut.a`) - `undefined === 1683.5` failed the check though the anchor had refined correctly (the before/after dump proved it: lon 0.2994483->0.2997432, mpx 0.420531->0.420441, rot 1->0.999864). Fixed to read under `.a`.
2. "pin: the sixth pair is the click" expected 1e-7 equality between the pinned pair's lon/lat and unproject of the requested pixel - but the browser QUANTIZES CDP mouse points to whole pixels before the DOM (measured across diag3-6: requested (1004.891, 385.000) -> clientX 1004, offsetX 1005; (1004.886, 385.000) -> the MapLibre event point (1004, 385), a 0.89px/0.001px shift, transform provably static). MapLibre 5.6's MapMouseEvent computes `point = n.mousePos(canvas, e) = (clientX - rect.left)/scale - clientLeft` (vendor getScale/getPoint) from that quantized DOM event, so the page's pin pair is the unproject of an integer pixel ~1px from my float. A physical mouse is quantized identically, the doc rounds to 7dp at save, and the fit is a least squares over several points - so this is not a product defect. The check now bounds the difference by 2x the per-pixel lng/lat step (measured in-page from two unprojects 2px apart). The committed part-4 test must encode the same tolerance, not exact equality.
3. The run-2 cancelOut evaluate referenced `site` (a probe-local) inside the page context -> ReferenceError. Fixed by passing `{site}` as the single evaluate argument.

### 2026-10-13 308 DECISION: CORRECTION + fix found - my position:relative on .marker overrode the vendor's .maplibregl-marker absolute parking; the huge anchor deltas were a CSS cascade bug, not globe projection
The iter-213 "KEY FINDING" (MapLibre globe: the marker's own transform carries the on-globe position; map.project() is the flat plane, up to ~3023px apart) was a MISDIAGNOSIS of this CSS bug. Measured this session: the transform point and map.project() agree within 0.35px (the transform IS the 2D-plane position). The huge rect-vs-transform deltas came from the marker elements being in NORMAL FLOW: my 308 CSS `.marker { ... position: relative }` (specificity 0,1,0, in the page's inline style which loads AFTER the vendor <link>) overrode the vendor's `.maplibregl-marker { left: 0; position: absolute; top: 0; }` (same specificity, earlier in the cascade). MapLibre parks marker elements at the canvas origin and places them purely with the inline transform; in flow, each marker stacks below the previous one in DOM order, so the transform lands it 500-3023px below its site. Proof by A/B (pre-308 0470610 served from /tmp/aw308before, port 44269, vs current, port 33187): BEFORE - all 324 shown markers in-view in globe/default (98-100 in zoom), rect-minus-transform = one constant 9.5px (the old square's anchor geometry, its border-box/content-box mismatch); AFTER (broken) - only 61/324 in-view in globe, flow offsets 505-3023px (Orkney markers with negative plane Y pushed into view, the Wiltshire markers that should be visible pushed off-window). The broken after-globe/zoom shots are artifacts of this bug, NOT globe behaviour.
Fix (applied to web/index.html, UNCOMMITTED at context limit): `.marker { ...; position: absolute; top: 0; left: 0; }` restating the vendor rule explicitly, with a comment explaining why it must not be a flowing position. Verified: rect-minus-transform = 0/0 for every shown marker in default/zoom/globe (the .ah box has border:0 so the anchor is exact); inView back to 324/324 (globe/default) and 98 (zoom).
Full probe re-run after the fix, ALL GREEN: shape 499/499 site markers + 328/328 legend + 324/324 list rows carry the arrowhead svg (scan areas: 0 on page, code untouched); anchorZoom n=98 worstTransform 0 / worstProject 0.69px; anchorGlobe n=324 worstTransform 0 / worstProject 0.68px; worstTipBelow 0.15px (visual stroke tip vs svg box bottom); click opens the site (aalsum). ## 2026-10-11 801 DECISION: offline candidate prototype done - extractor rules finalized (NFKD mandatory; pairs-before-singles order; title-only-pass rejected)
Iter 16 (agent c). Built /tmp/sheet_proto.py (v1) and /tmp/sheet_proto2.py (v2, throwaway, no repo
changes) and eyeballed ALL 354 stored-none rows per site against the iter-14 census. Findings that
changed the iter-15 design:
1. NFKD-normalize BEFORE tokenizing - mandatory. v1 tokenized raw text: "Orléans" -> "O"+"rl"+"ans"
   (zero candidates), which would have cost the 4 cenabum pass rows; "Bethléem"/"Maastricht" variants
   likewise. Candidates are stored in the normalized form (the check's norm-substring test stays
   valid because check() normalizes both sides).
2. Strip the "File:" prefix and truncate desc at a word boundary at 600 chars (a cut word like
   "Bethl" becomes a phantom candidate otherwise). Digits are never kept tokens (v1 bug: "000",
   "1870" leaked and formed junk pairs).
3. Run splitting: a comma OR a real lowercase word (len>=3) between two kept words breaks the run.
   Keeps "New Orleans" / "Cranbourne Hampshire" / "Monmouth Castle" as phrases while breaking OS
   place lists (v1's greedy 3-merge turned them into unresolvable garbage and lost the singles).
4. Candidate order per run: 2-word pairs, then 3-word phrases, then singles. Decisive: the lone
   "Orleans" resolves to Orléans (the cenabum site itself); trying it before "New Orleans" would
   FALSE-PASS the New-Orleans junk rows. Pairs-first prevents that.
5. Verdict = the existing caption-route best/conflict logic over the candidate set (nearest <=50 km
   -> sheet_mention pass; nearest far -> none+conflict; else plain none). Title-preference for
   PASSES was tested and rejected: the cenabum New-Orleans junk names the place only in the DESC and
   box 2 demands the conflict there.
6. STOP list mined from the 354 rows' capitalized-word frequency table (EN metadata labels + NL/FR
   field words + adjectives English/Roman/...); NEVER stop place-name components (New, Great, Old,
   North/South, City, Church, Tower, River, Park, Garden). v2's list accidentally DROPPED the
   preposition block (The/Of/De/Van/La/Le...) and "ordnance/quartier/house/design/pattern/textile/
   numerisation/onderdeel" - those additions + the digit exclusion are still PENDING (my edit call
   failed atomically); they are listed in the task hand-over.
Expected after the fixes: ~1400-1600 unique candidates (v2 measured 2078); the tail is person names
(authors/artists/publishers of the ~180 book-scan rows) - harmless (no P625, the distance guard is
the mechanism), just one-off search cost (~25-35 min at 1 req/s).
Accepted consequence (logged per the iter-14 rule): a city name shared with a person/family name
("York" on the 1914 Christmas tin on york-castle, "Dudley" on a genealogy book) will pass when the
site sits in that city - keyword+50km cannot distinguish a depiction from a name mention; the
never-pass-far guarantee holds and box 1 only needs the majority of the genuinely-naming rows (the
40 Clifford rows pass via the part route, which runs before sheet).
Part-route check: EXACTLY 40 of the 354 none rows name a has_part of their own site (all
Clifford's Tower) - matches the iter-15 census.

## 2026-10-11 801 DECISION: sheet verdict is a FIRST-RESOLVED WALK, not "nearest <=50 km wins" (iter-16's two statements were contradictory)
Iter 17 (agent c). Iter-16 said both "nearest <=50 km -> pass; nearest far -> conflict" and "pairs-before-
singles prevents the New-Orleans false pass". Both true only if the walk is order-dependent: iterate the
ordered candidates (per run: pairs, then 3-word phrases, then singles; title before desc) and let the
FIRST candidate that resolves decide the row (<=50 km pass / >50 km conflict); unresolved candidates are
skipped. Verified the "nearest wins" variant is WRONG on three real rows: "York" (a word inside "New
York") resolves ~2 km from york-castle and would pass the 4 NYC "Castle Garden" rows; "Orleans" (inside
"New Orleans") resolves onto cenabum itself and would pass the 13 New-Orleans rows; "York Castle" (glued
from "New York. Castle Garden") resolves to the site itself and would pass the same 4 rows. Routes cascade
caption -> part -> sheet; the first route returning pass or conflict decides (a caption conflict preempts
sheet, e.g. the 2 "detail Limmel" rows whose caption names "Bethlehem" -> Q5776 ~4700 km; a 3rd Limmel row
without that word still conflicts, because Maastricht is ~290 km from bethlehem-q2523914's stored point -
6.61E 53.38N is NOT near Maastricht).

## 2026-10-11 801 DECISION: castrum-levefanum is the DUTCH Limes fort, not Beauvais - the "Peutinger Casaromago" rows conflict on BOTH limes sites (census correction)

castrum-levefanum "~Beauvais". Wrong: the catalog site (Q1309559) is stored at (5.353E, 51.963N) - the
Dutch Lower German Limes identification (region netherlands, part_of Q1265889), 314-368 km from
Beauvais/Amiens. Live-checked this session (3 small wbsearchentities/wbgetentities queries): "Casaromago"
and "Sammarobriva" have NO Wikidata items (search returns []), and "Peutinger" first-P625 is Q2081791
(Peutinger-Gymnasium Ellwangen, 10.13E 48.97N) = 475-500 km from both Dutch sites. So the first-resolved

# Task 804 fit-queue-wire

## 2026-10-12 804 DECISION: iteration 100 (session 9) - the two-phase right-place wiring landed in tools/fit_queue.py (boxes 1+2) and verified on real data: 15 flags == CLI, queue 116->114, 5 new review items / 6 upserts carrying place_reason, steady-state zero churn; the code is UNCOMMITTED at hand-over (harness-saved) - the next session commits it first
Session 9 on the 309 lane. Worked 804 boxes 1+2 (the wiring itself) in the working tree on top of the session-8 refactor (d413d0e); the context limit hit before the commit, so the tools/fit_queue.py diff is harness-saved and UNCOMMITTED - git status at hand-over shows exactly that one modified file (no data files, no agent-a files).
1. What landed: header docstring (the namesake rule; the stdlib-only line names right_place/review as the only imports); self sys.path inserts of ROOT/tools and ROOT/fit before `import right_place` / `import review` (noqa E402, the site_done pattern - required under the runpy GUARD, PITFALLS); _site_records (sites.json keyed by id, site_facts' input); _place_store (right_place.load, None when none of catalog/index/lists present -> build is exactly 305's, the no-op degrade); _place_flags (one site_facts per site, picture_facts+check_pairing per candidate, over the PRE-MUTATION maps -> {(sid, plan): (facts, reason)}); _item_candidate; _place_entry (the item's stored fields as a dict copy when item-origin - pairs/evidence/why travel with it - else the row's fields, batch_us._entry's shape with the books/<ia>/<file> url fallback; plus plan and the reason under the NEW key place_reason); _apply_flags (sorted flag order: drop the plan, a site emptied leaves the queue; top of find_right_site (min_score 0.5) = T: T queue-eligible -> dict-copy of the row with sites narrowed to [T] joins T's map, else upsert into T's item (or S's own item when no passing T), SKIPPED when that item already holds the plan; a per-build moved set stops duplicate (target, plan) writes); build() = maps -> store (None -> no-op) -> flags -> apply -> _entry; final sort and {at, entries} envelope untouched; the build never calls review.export and never removes a candidate from an item.
2. Design decisions (refinements of the box wording, all deliberate): (a) "T is built" for the join-entry branch = T is queue-ELIGIBLE (in sites.json + dir exists + no hand doc, the eligible set from built/hand), not merely "web/data/sites/<T>/ exists" as box 2's words say - a move into a hand-fit site (or a dir absent from sites.json) has no entry to join and would silently lose the candidate; the refinement is inert on today's data (every right site is unbuilt) and box 4's synthetic test covers the entry branch. (b) The reason's key is place_reason - a new extra (the batch's why/gate_score stay untouched; a candidate can carry both); the 804 box-3 README note documents it, and 307c (agent a) will display it from this key. (c) The never-rewrite-held-item skip (box 2's steady-state rule, specified only for S's own item) was extended to the T-item branch too: a batch's own entry in a T item carries pairs/evidence/coarse that the thinner move entry would erase, and a re-run's entry is byte-identical anyway, so skipping is exactly the no-churn steady state the box wants. (d) The build never removes a flagged candidate from the source item (the "both stay in review forever" decision stands) - the flag+drop is recomputed from stored fields every build, so the queue stays clean indefinitely.
3. Verification (all in temp trees; the checkout's data stayed untouched): (i) part-1 tests pass UNMODIFIED in 0.68 s (the synthetic tree has no catalog/books = pure no-op; the current four-inputs-only test_fit_queue_real is a no-op too); (ii) real data (four 305 inputs + data/catalog + data/books, build() run in-process twice): the build's flags == the CLI's set EXACTLY (15; `python3 tools/right_place.py --all` on the checkout still 324 checked / 15 flagged); queue 116 -> 114 entries (vindomora and windmill-hill leave entirely - every candidate flagged; devil-s-dyke keeps only n0662_1, the owner's Brighton case out of the Cambridgeshire dyke's entry; bokerley-dyke keeps n0174_1; must-not-flag set untouched); EXACTLY 5 new review-item files / 6 upserts each with place_reason and the row's url (saucer-barrow...n-q17677473 gets n0558_1 AND n0558_2, castle-dyke-q31112898 n0599_1, devil-s-dyke-hillfort-q17674160 n0686_1, down-end-castle-q5302812 n0285_1, oval-barrow...-q17672356 n0557_1 - 805's rebuild must reproduce exactly these); 341 existing item files unchanged; the second build's queue is identical (ex-at) and every item file byte-identical (zero churn); (iii) full suite `.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/ -q`: 3 failed / 77 passed / 1 skipped = baseline (the same three pre-existing main-side failures; no new failures).
